verdicts.title: A Note on the LogRank Conjecture in Communication Complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The LogRank conjecture of Lovász and Saks (1988) is the most famous open problem in communication complexity theory. The statement is as follows: suppose that two players intend to compute a Boolean function f(x,y) when x is known for the first and y for the second player, and they may send and receive messages encoded with bits, then they can compute f(x,y) with exchanging (log rank(Mf))c bits, where Mf is a Boolean matrix, determined by function f.
